Use a separate output model that doesn't include the password field, and set it as the `response_model`. FastAPI will take care of filtering out all the data that is not declared in the output model (using Pydantic).[1]

```python
class UserIn(BaseModel):
    username: str
    password: str
    email: EmailStr
    full_name: str | None = None


class UserOut(BaseModel):
    username: str
    email: EmailStr
    full_name: str | None = None


@app.post("/user/", response_model=UserOut)
async def create_user(user: UserIn) -> Any:
    return user
```

The function can still return an object that contains the password (here it returns `UserIn`). Because `UserOut` has no password field, the password is stripped from the response. The same approach works for a hashed password field.

If you also have a return type annotation, keep in mind that if you declare both a return type and a `response_model`, the `response_model` will take priority and be used by FastAPI.[2] So make sure `response_model` points to the model without the password.
